title: Box Plot vs Violin Plot Selection
description: Selection criteria between Tukey box plots and kernel density violin plots for group distribution comparison.
conditions: Comparing a continuous metric across discrete categories or cohorts
Displaying median, quartiles, and outlier points simultaneously
recommended_methods: Standard Tukey Box Plot with IQR whiskers and individual outlier points
Violin Plot with embedded box plot or quartile lines
Strip plot / Jitter overlay on box plot for small sample sizes (N < 50 per group)
selection_rules: If group sample size N < 30, use Box Plot with jittered data points, NOT Violin Plot
If distribution is suspected to be bimodal or multimodal within groups, use Violin Plot (box plots hide bimodal shapes)
Sort categories along the categorical axis by median value for instant cognitive readability
limitations: Box plots hide the distribution's actual sample size and modality completely
Violin plots are frequently misunderstood by non-technical executive stakeholders
